title: split-gpu-pools-per-az-and-tenant-and-align-tfstate-backends
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Private installs running multiple tenants in a single VPC have inconsistent GPU nodepool placement and a monolithic tfstate layout which complicates upgrades and tenant-scoped disaster recovery. This PR splits GPU nodepools by availability zone and tenant boundary, creates a per-tenant tfstate backend layout with migration tooling, and tightens IAM bindings so nodepools have least-privilege access to cloud resources. Changeset summary: new module modules/gpu-nodepool/v2 supports az-aware subpool creation; modules/state introduces per-tenant backend config templates and a migrator helper script; modules/iam adds role-per-nodepool and conditional bindings for nodepool identity vs cluster identity; networking updates ensure subnet allocation ranges are parameterized per-az to allow fine-grained nodepool placement. Migration strategy: includes an automated terraform state migrator script (scripts/tfstate-migrator.sh) that iteratively snapshots, copies state to tenant-specific S3 paths, and verifies plan-idempotence before switching backends. Rollout plan: 1) run migrator in dry-run mode for a single canary tenant, 2) create AZ-split nodepools in canary tenant with drain/cordon sequences, 3) shift workloads and validate perf/latency, 4) repeat per-tenant, 5) decommission legacy pooled resources when all tenants migrated. Rollback plan: revert to previous backend by re-pointing workspace to original S3 prefix and reimporting resources using documented import steps; node replacement is non-destructive so failure during nodepool creation can be rolled back by draining new pools and reattaching workloads to previous pools. Testing: added unit tests for backend interpolation logic and new terratest scenarios in tests/ that validate resource counts per-az and IAM role bindings. Impact and compatibility: no changes to public APIs; operators must run migrator once per environment; terraform state locking is preserved via existing DynamoDB locks. Security notes: new IAM roles follow least-privilege and require an explicit admin approval gate in the console to enable cross-tenant nodepool creation. Related work: ENG-3142 (tenant-scoped infra isolation), ENG-3220 (gpu scheduling improvements). See files_changed for detailed diffs.

release_notes: Private deploy: Split GPU nodepools by AZ and tenant; introduce per-tenant tfstate backends and automated migrator; add nodepool-scoped IAM roles; parameterized subnets per AZ; operators must run migrator once per environment; see upgrade guide for steps.
testing_notes: Local terratest flow: export TEST_AWS_BUCKET and TEST_AWS_DYNAMODB, run make test-terratest-target with GINKGO_PARALLEL=1. CI runs a mocked prod plan to ensure no drift. Migrator has --dry-run and --apply flags; always run dry-run and checksum verification before apply.
upgrade_guide: Operators: 1) read docs/migrator-usage.md and ensure administrative approval for IAM role rollout, 2) run scripts/tfstate-migrator.sh --dry-run --tenant <canary-tenant> and verify checksum output, 3) apply GPU nodepool v2 module for canary tenant with terraform apply, 4) validate workload behavior and run terratest suite, 5) for full rollout iterate tenants, 6) revert by re-pointing backend prefix and reimporting resources if needed; full rollback instructions in docs/rollback-tfstate.md.
